stem.en: Why can one run of distillation not give you all five parts of lemonade?

text.en: Lemonade is a solution, and nothing can ever be taken out of a solution by any method.
Distillation only works on two liquids, so nothing would come over from lemonade.
It uses one difference: water comes over, and the other parts stay behind together.
The sugar comes over with the water, so the liquid in the receiver is still sweet.

explanation.en: Distillation uses a difference in boiling point. Water boils off, and sugar, acid, colour and pulp stay in the flask together. Option a is the tempting one, but distillation takes pure water out of salt water, so a solution can be separated. It also works on salt water, which is not two liquids. Sugar does not turn to vapour, so the distillate is plain water.
